hints.content:
### Definition of cosine

For an angle with measure $\theta$ in a right triangle:

$\cos(\theta)=\dfrac{\goldE{\text{adjacent leg length}}}{\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$

### Identifying the hypotenuse and the side adjacent to $\angle A$

The side $\goldE{\text{adjacent}}$ to $\angle A$ is $\overline{AC}$ and its length is $\goldE{21}$ units.

The $\purpleD{\text{hypotenuse}}$ is $\overline{AB}$ and its length is $\purpleD{29}$ units.

But $\cos(\alpha)$ is the side *adjacent* to $\angle A$ divided by the hypotenuse.
